_meta.name: Luganda
_meta.note: Standard written Luganda in the neutral register of Uganda Ministry of Health (Minisitule y'Ebyobulamu) public-health messages and Luganda news media, using current orthography (r only after e and i, doubled consonants); technical terms with no settled Luganda equivalent are paraphrased or kept as loanwords in common Ugandan use (modeli, data, laboratole, maapu, lipooti, API key). Four verbs are kept apart: 'okukakasa' only for official or laboratory confirmation (abakakasiddwa), 'okwekebejja' for verifying unofficial reports and transport status, 'okukebera obutuufu' for validating official figures and 'okwetegereza' for human review, while 'okwekenneenya' is severity assessment. Case classes are abakakasiddwa (confirmed) / abalabika okuba ne Ebola (probable) / abateeberezebwa (suspected); 'ekigeraageranyo' (estimate) is never used for 'omuwendo omutongole' (official figure); 'obubonero' is reserved for symptoms, so unofficial signals are 'amawulire agatali matongole'. Severity level names form an ordinal scale (Okwegendereza < Waggulu katono < Waggulu < Waggulu nnyo) under the noun 'obuzito', and confidence uses Wansi nnyo / Wansi / Wakati / Waggulu under the separate noun 'obwesige', because the interface uses one string for 'High'. Nested phrases are inserted after a colon or in parentheses so that noun-class agreement does not break.
